land.text: Guria on the Black Sea, one of the 'western provinces' George VIII lost after the Battle of Chikhori in 1463

predecessors.note: The page also lists the Kingdom of Imereti as a predecessor and calls Guria its client state from the 1460s; the land came from the united kingdom, and Imereti's overlordship is recorded in the Imereti dossier.

land.text: Guria, deposed by Russia on 2 September 1829 and made the Ozurgeti uyezd of Kutais Governorate in 1840 (without Adjara, which Russia took from the Ottomans in 1878)

successors.note: Annexation date 2 September 1829 (infobox); Cliopatria ends the row in 1829.

capitals.name: Ozurgeti
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Ozurgeti, with no years given; coordinates are the modern town's.

correction.text: Guria as it stands in Cliopatria's first shape, carried back to 1463

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Guria in 1468 but the page puts the break from the Georgian crown in the 1460s ('In 1463, Bagrat defeated the king at Chikhori, and George VIII lost the western provinces'), and the infobox dates the feudal wars 1463. The 1468 shape is carried back unchanged.

4,181 km2. 'In 1491, Giorgi I Gurieli was recognized as a sovereign prince.' The page gives no area, so the size cannot be compared; the shape is a modest Black Sea strip around Ozurgeti, which fits a principality of 22 princes. At the 11-cell Ajaria grid the shape holds 9 of Ajaria's 11 cells, which fits the page's 'southern provinces of Adjara' before the 1540s.

4,827 km2; the only early shape that reaches into Turkey (one grid cell at about 41.47N 42.05E, the Machakhela valley). The page names Machakheli as a southern province 'which had earlier been acquired by Rostom Gurieli (1534-64)' and annexed by the Ottomans in the 1540s, so the page gives no Gurian hold there in 1507-1515 (Giorgi I Gurieli ruled 1483-1512). The cell is removed, which makes the shape equal to 1516's. The shape also adds two inland Ajaria cells to 1468's (about 500 km2, 4,181 to 4,827 km2 in all); the page is silent, and they stay because the page puts Adjara in Guria until the 1540s. The Machakheli acquisition is undated within 1534-64 and is not ledgered.

correction.text: the 1507 shape without its cell in Turkey, i.e. the 1516 shape, for 1507-1515

keyframe_review.note: 4,659 km2, Georgia only; at the grid it holds all 11 cells of Ajaria (Adjara). The page says nothing on 1516-1546; kept. The page puts Adjara in Guria until the Ottoman annexation of the 1540s.

4,300 km2 (-8%) in Cliopatria, but the grid shows that the shape loses only the two Batumi coast cells and adds a cell in Turkey: it still holds 9 of Ajaria's 11 cells. The page has the Ottomans annex 'its southern provinces of Adjara, Northern Chaneti ..., and Machakheli' in the 1540s (decade only; 1547 is Cliopatria's year) and Adjara stays out until Mamia II's 1609 reconquest; the Adjara page gives no 1540s date and says the Ottomans held Adjara to 1878, and russian-empire takes Ajaria only in 1878. Corrected by taking all of Ajaria and the Turkish cell out; this is the land of /ledger/1.

correction.text: Guria without Adjara and without Machakheli: 'in the 1540s, ... annexed its southern provinces of Adjara, Northern Chaneti (latter-day Lazistan), and Machakheli' (the 1547 shape without Ajaria and Turkey), held to 1608
the 1547 shape without Ajaria and Turkey, i.e. Guria without the southern provinces annexed by the Ottomans in the 1540s, held until 1608

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria restores the lost western strip in 1564-1571 (4,659 km2, all of Ajaria again), but the page has the Ottomans holding the southern provinces from the 1540s until Mamia II 'reconquered Adjara in 1609'. Nothing on the page supports a return in 1564. The corrected 1547 shape (without Ajaria and the Turkish cell) is used for 1564-1571.

4,300 km2, the same cells as the 1547 shape (9 of Ajaria's 11 cells and one Turkish cell). Consistent with the page only after Adjara and the Turkish cell are taken out: the Ottomans hold the southern provinces from the 1540s to 1609. The Cliopatria gap 1579-1611 is filled by the new keyframes below.

correction.text: the 1572 shape without Ajaria and Turkey, i.e. the same corrected shape as 1547, held until 1608
Guria without Adjara and Machakheli, 1579-1608; from 1609 the 1612 shape applies

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria leaves empty (1579-1611), probably because its Ottoman row covers them (that row holds all 11 Ajaria cells in 1580-1600). The page does not break Guria's life: Mamia II ruled 1600-1625, and the Gurieli never lose their principality before 1829. The corrected 1547 shape (Ottomans holding Adjara) is kept to 1608; the 1609 reconquest of Adjara is an event.

correction.text: the 1612 shape (Guria with Adjara's coast) from Mamia II's reconquest of Adjara in 1609

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1609-1611: 'Mamia II Gurieli (1600-1625) reconquered Adjara in 1609'. The 1612 shape (which includes the coast to 41.58E) applies three years early.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1612-1614 only (Guria with all of Adjara); from 1615 the shape without inland Adjara applies

keyframe_review.note: 4,659 km2, all 11 cells of Ajaria, for 1612-1614: Adjara is Gurian from the 1609 reconquest until Mamia II 'was eventually forced to renounce, on December 13, 1614, any claims to the region and to pay an annual tribute to the Sublime Porte'. Shape unchanged, years shortened to 1612-1614; the renunciation is /ledger/3, and the 1615-1722 keyframe below takes inland Adjara out. correction.text: Guria after the renunciation of 13 December 1614 of 'any claims to the region': the 1612 shape without inland Adjara (Ajaria minus the five coastal cells that the 1727 shape loses), so with the coast of Batumi, Chakvi and Kobuleti, 1615-1722

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 11 grid cells (about 2,800 km2 at the grid): inland Adjara (the 8 Ajaria cells that the 1727 shape keeps) is out, because Mamia II renounced 'any claims to the region' on 13 December 1614, the Adjara page has the Ottomans conquering the area in 1614 and holding it to 1878, and russian-empire takes Ajaria only in 1878. The coast stays because the page has the Gurieli losing Batumi and Chakvi only 'by 1723'. That split is a reading of two sentences that do not mention each other; if Batumi and Chakvi went with the rest in 1614, this shape should lose the five coastal cells in 1615 and /ledger/4 would be a confirmation.

correction.text: Guria without Batumi and Chakvi and without Adjara: 'By 1723, the Gurieli had lost Batumi and Chakvi to the Ottomans' (the 1727 shape without Ajaria and Turkey, plus the Kobuleti coast, which stays until the 1768-1774 war), valid 1723-1771

keyframe_review.note: 3,823 km2 (-18%) in Cliopatria: the coast from Batumi to Ureki goes in five grid cells, and 8 Ajaria cells plus a Turkish cell stay in the shape. 'By 1723, the Gurieli had lost Batumi and Chakvi to the Ottomans' and 'the whole coastline of Guria had been garrisoned by the Turks'. Corrected: years 1723-1771; inland Adjara and the Turkish cell out; the two Kobuleti cells put back until 1772, because the page has Kobuleti 'detached from Guria' only in the war of 1768-1774 (garrisoned is not detached). The Ureki-Supsa coast cell stays lost from 1723.

3,728 km2 (-2.5%) in Cliopatria, the same grid cells as the 1727 shape. 'During the Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774), Gurian support for Russia prompted an Ottoman reaction, and Kobuleti was detached from Guria.' The Guria page gives the war, not a year; the war page (opened 2026-10-31) does not mention Guria or Kobuleti (it has the failed Russo-Georgian siege of Poti in 1771 and the Russian withdrawal in spring 1772), so 1772 stays Cliopatria's year. Inland Adjara and the Turkish cell are taken out as in the earlier keyframes.

correction.text: the 1772 shape without Ajaria and Turkey: Guria after Kobuleti was 'detached from Guria and subjected to Islamization', 1772-1810

keyframe_review.note: 3,776 km2 for 1811-1827: 'on June 19, 1810, Mamia V accepted Russian suzerainty, becoming an autonomous principality.' The territory does not change on the page; the 1% shape change in 1811 is not explained. Guria stays a Russian vassal to 1829. Adjara (Ottoman until 1878 per the Adjara page and russian-empire) and the Turkish cell are taken out.

correction.text: the 1811 shape without Ajaria and Turkey, 1811-1827

keyframe_review.note: 3,776 km2, 1828-1829. 'Sophia sided with the Turks during the Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)'; Russia deposed David on 2 September 1829 (Guria page); the Treaty of Adrianople of 14 September 1829 has the Sultan recognize Russia's possession of 'Georgia (with Imeretia, Mingrelia, Guria)'. Cliopatria ends the row in 1829, as the page does. Adjara and the Turkish cell are taken out (Ottoman until 1878).

correction.text: the 1828 shape without Ajaria and Turkey, 1828-1829

region.text: Guria around Ozurgeti on the Black Sea, the Gurieli's principality 'from the 1460s'

ledger.note: 1463: the Gurieli make Guria independent of the Georgian crown. 'In the 1460s, the Vardanisdze-Gurieli dynasty joined a rebellion led by Bagrat against King George VIII'; 'In 1463, Bagrat defeated the king at Chikhori, and George VIII lost the western provinces'; 'In 1491, Giorgi I Gurieli was recognized as a sovereign prince.' The infobox calls Guria a client state of Imereti from the 1460s.

region.text: its southern provinces of Adjara, Northern Chaneti (latter-day Lazistan), and Machakheli

ledger.note: 1540s: the Ottomans take the south of Guria. 'In the 1540s, the Ottomans imposed a naval blockade on Guria and annexed its southern provinces of Adjara, Northern Chaneti (latter-day Lazistan), and Machakheli, which had earlier been acquired by Rostom Gurieli (1534-64).' The page names only the decade (the Adjara page, opened 2026-10-31 to look for a year, has no 1540s sentence); 1547 is the year of Cliopatria's shape change. The region is Adjara only, the land the keyframes move; Lazistan and Machakheli lie outside the Gurian shapes.

region.text: Adjara, reconquered by Mamia II Gurieli

ledger.note: 1609: Mamia II Gurieli retakes Adjara from the Ottomans. 'Mamia II Gurieli (1600-1625) managed to reconquer Adjara in 1609, but was eventually forced to renounce, on December 13, 1614, any claims to the region and to pay an annual tribute to the Sublime Porte.' The renunciation is the next event.

13 December 1614: Mamia II renounces Adjara to the Ottomans. 'Mamia II Gurieli (1600-1625) managed to reconquer Adjara in 1609, but was eventually forced to renounce, on December 13, 1614, any claims to the region and to pay an annual tribute to the Sublime Porte.' The Adjara page agrees: 'The Ottomans conquered the area in 1614.' Date and event are the page's; the region is inland Adjara (Ajaria without the coastal cells of Batumi, Chakvi and Kobuleti), because the page has Batumi and Chakvi lost only 'by 1723' (next event). Gurian tribute to the Porte from this date is for the Ottoman dossier.

region.text: By 1723, the Gurieli had lost Batumi and Chakvi to the Ottomans

ledger.note: By 1723 the Ottomans hold Batumi and Chakvi and garrison the coast. 'By 1723, the Gurieli had lost Batumi and Chakvi to the Ottomans, and the whole coastline of Guria had been garrisoned by the Turks.' The page gives no earlier year; Cliopatria's shape changes in 1727. The region is the coast cells that Cliopatria's 1727 shape loses (Batumi and Chakvi, and the Ureki-Supsa coast) without the Kobuleti cells, which the page detaches only in 1768-1774 (next ledger event).

region.text: Kobuleti, detached from Guria in the Ottoman reaction to Gurian support for Russia

ledger.note: 1772: Kobuleti is cut from Guria after Guria backs Russia. 'During the Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774), Gurian support for Russia prompted an Ottoman reaction, and Kobuleti was detached from Guria.' The page gives the war, not the year, and the war page is silent on Kobuleti; 1772 is Cliopatria's shape year (its shape equals the 1727 one at the grid, so the keyframes keep Kobuleti to 1771 and take it out here).

region.text: the whole principality, deposed by Russia on 2 September 1829

ledger.note: 1829: Russia deposes Prince David and annexes Guria. 'On September 2, 1829, Russia deposed David and exiled Sophia to Turkey' (infobox: annexation by Imperial Russia, September 2, 1829); in 1840 Guria became the Ozurgeti uyezd of Kutais Governorate.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Gurian support for Russia prompted an Ottoman reaction and Kobuleti was detached from Guria (Guria page); the Imereti side of the war is in the Imereti dossier.
wars.note: The Guria page does not say who held Kobuleti afterwards; the Ottomans are inferred from 'an Ottoman reaction'. No contest events: the page records a transfer, not a held front.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: 'On June 19, 1810, Mamia V accepted Russian suzerainty, becoming an autonomous principality' (Guria page). The Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) returned Poti, Anapa and Akhalkalaki to Turkey and left Guria's status untouched (war page lists Guria only among belligerents).
wars.note: No territorial change in Guria itself is dated by either page.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: Princess Sophia of Guria sided with the Turks; Russia deposed Prince David on 2 September 1829 and the Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) had the Sultan recognize Russia's possession of 'Georgia (with Imeretia, Mingrelia, Guria)'.
wars.note: Guria page for the deposition; the treaty page for the recognition. No fighting on Guria's land is described.

certainty.note: A small principality between the Ottoman coast and Imereti; no treaty line or survey on the pages. The Ottoman coastal frontier (Adjara, Batumi, Kobuleti) moved several times and is approximate throughout.

notes: Page budget: up to 5 pages, five opened, plus two for the repair (Adjara; Russo-Turkish War 1768-1774). Infobox area absent, so no area comparison is possible; shapes judged on dated sentences and, for Adjara, on the grid cells. Cliopatria quirks: (1) the Guria shapes hold 9-11 of the 11 grid cells of Ajaria (Adjara) in every year 1468-1829 and a cell in Turkey (Machakhela valley) in 1507-1515, 1547-1578 and 1727-1829, although the page has the Ottomans annexing Adjara, Northern Chaneti and Machakheli in the 1540s, Mamia II reconquering Adjara in 1609 and renouncing 'any claims to the region' on 13 December 1614, and Russia taking Ajaria from the Ottomans only in 1878 (russian-empire ledger); all shapes are corrected by taking Ajaria and Turkey out except 1468-1546 and 1609-1614 (Adjara Gurian) and 1615-1722 (inland Adjara out, coast kept); (2) the 1564-1571 shape restores the western strip (adjusted to the 1547 correction); (3) 1612-1726 includes the coast to 41.58E, while the page has Batumi and Chakvi lost 'by 1723' (the 1612 shape stops in 1614, a 1615-1722 keyframe drops inland Adjara, the 1727 shape applies from 1723); (4) Cliopatria has no shape for 1579-1611 (filled with new keyframes; its Ottoman row holds all of Ajaria in 1580-1600); (5) the 1727 shape drops the whole coast from Batumi to Ureki in one move, so the Kobuleti cells are put back until 1771, as the page dates the Kobuleti detachment to the war of 1768-1774. Reading to check: 1614 against 1723. The page has Mamia renounce Adjara in 1614 yet lose Batumi and Chakvi 'by 1723'; I keep the coast to 1722 (confidence 2); if both went in 1614 the 1615-1722 keyframe should lose the coastal cells in 1615. Machakheli was acquired by Rostom Gurieli (1534-64), undated, and is not ledgered. Vassalage, for the dossiers of the suzerains (the Guria page and its sources give these dates): Imereti's client state from the 1460s to 1810 (infobox; Imereti dossier records it); Ottoman tributary from 13 December 1614 (Mamia II 'was eventually forced to renounce ... any claims to the region and to pay an annual tribute to the Sublime Porte'); Russian suzerainty from 19 June 1810 ('Mamia V accepted Russian suzerainty, becoming an autonomous principality') to 2 September 1829; Cliopatria's Russian Empire row neighbours Guria 1803-1829. Counterpart gaps for the Ottoman dossier: it has Ajaria pass from Imereti in 1555 (its /ledger/80, 'the researcher's reading') and no event for the 1540s annexation from Guria, the 1609 loss, the 1614 recovery or the 1723 coast. Region names the gazetteer may lack: Kobuleti (place). Founding: the infobox dates the feudal wars 1463; 1491 is the date of sovereign recognition. The Gurieli and the page give no ruler list, so no rulers strip.
